# Basic Python (12 points)

## Columbia Courses

Create a list that has the course abbreviations (letters and numbers) for all the courses that you have completed at Columbia, not including this semester. You should assign it to a symbol.

## List Extension

Modify the list (in place) that you created in the previous subproblem to include the course abbreviations for all of the classes that you are taking this semester.

## Months and Days

Create a dictionary whose keys are the months and whose values are the number of days in the corresponding month in 2026. You should assign it to a symbol.

## Leap Years

Now presume it is a leap year like 2028. Modify the dictionary that you created in the previous problem to include the correct number of days in February.

# Using Pandas (12 points)

First, read this Wikipedia article on how Gross Domestic Product can be measured

<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product>

We are going to compare real quarterly growth rates between what Wikipedia calls "the expenditure approach (GDP)" and "the income approach (GDI)".

Execute the following to download that data from the United States Federal Reserve.

```{python}
import pandas as pd

url = ("https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv"
       "?id=A191RL1Q225SBEA,A261RL1Q225SBEA")
growth = pd.read_csv(url,
                     header=0, 
                     names=["quarter", "gdp_growth", "gdi_growth"],
                     parse_dates=["quarter"], 
                     index_col="quarter")

```

## Observations

How many observations are there and what is the date range that they span?

## Missing Values

How many values are missing on each of the variables in `growth`?

## Correlation

What is the correlation between the observed values of GDP growth and GDI growth?

## Gross Domestic Output

Many economists contend that the average of GDP growth and GDI growth is a more reliable measure of the change in output. Create a new column within `growth` called `gdo_growth` that computes this average.
